@@ -7,10 +7,40 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import re
 from html.parser import HTMLParser
 from urllib.parse import urlparse
 
 
+def _is_link_present(link: str, text: str) -> bool:
+    """Check if link is present in text with proper word boundary/delimiter handling.
+
+    A link counts as present only when some occurrence of it in the text is
+    immediately followed by: end of text; whitespace; one of `, ; : ! ? ) ] > " '`;
+    or a `.` that is itself followed by end of text or whitespace.
+    """
+    # Escape special regex characters in the link
+    escaped_link = re.escape(link)
+    # Match the link followed by either:
+    # - end of string ($)
+    # - whitespace (\s)
+    # - specific punctuation chars
+    # - a period followed by whitespace or end of string
+    pattern = (
+        escaped_link
+        + r"(?="
+        + r"$"  # end of text
+        + r"|"
+        + r"\s"  # whitespace
+        + r"|"
+        + r"[,;:!?\)\]>\"']"  # specific punctuation
+        + r"|"
+        + r"\.(?=\s|$)"  # period followed by whitespace or end
+        + r")"
+    )
+    return bool(re.search(pattern, text))
+
+

task.body: ## Problem `app/intake/html_links.py` treats a link as already present with a plain substring test (`link not in text`), both in `_LinkPreservingParser.text()` and in `merge_plain_with_html_links`. `https://example.org/paper/123` is therefore considered present when the text only contains `https://example.org/paper/1234` or `https://example.org/paper/123/supplement`, and its `Source URL:` line is lost. ## Required behaviour - A link counts as present only when some occurrence of it in the text is immediately followed by: end of text; whitespace; one of `, ; : ! ? ) ] > " '`; or a `.` that is itself followed by end of text or whitespace. - Apply this rule in both `_LinkPreservingParser.text()` and `merge_plain_with_html_links`. - HTML whose visible text is `Supplement: https://example.org/paper/123/supplement` plus a link `View Source` yields `'Supplement: https://example.org/paper/123/supplement\nView Source\nSource URL: https://example.org/paper/123'`. - `merge_plain_with_html_links` with plain text `Full text: https://example.org/paper/1234` and HTML linking `https://example.org/paper/123` returns `'Full text: https://example.org/paper/1234\n\nSource URL: https://example.org/paper/123'`. - `merge_plain_with_html_links("Source: https://example.org/source.", )` returns the plain text unchanged. - Existing tests are unchanged. ## Scope Allowed paths: - `app/intake/html_links.py` - `tests/test_intelligence_html_links.py` Do not change any other file. Existing tests must keep passing unchanged; add new tests only to the test file above. ## Validation - `python -m pytest -q tests/test_intelligence_html_links.py tests/test_twin_gmail_collector.py` - `python -m ruff check app/intake/html_links.py tests/test_intelligence_html_links.py` New tests must cover: - a prefix URL in the HTML visible text; - a prefix URL in the plain text for `merge_plain_with_html_links`; - a link followed by sentence punctuation still counts as present.
